validity.recommendation: no action on existence/classification/ownership; entity is real and correctly classified
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently. This is the gas export pipeline for Eni/NOC's Structures A and E gas fields development (Contractual Area D, offshore Libya) — FID taken Jan 2023 ($8bn investment, Mellitah Oil & Gas JV), first production targeted 2026, up to 750 MMscf/d. Source: sheet's own cited offshore-technology.com project page (verified live) plus Eni's own Jan-2023 press release (verified live) confirm the project and its Eni(50%)/NOC(50%) ownership independently of GEM. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is reasonable — this is the dedicated gas export line from field to onshore treatment, not a local gathering/process line. FUEL=Gas confirmed via mellitahog.ly (existing ref, verified). OWNERSHIP: Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp 50% / Owner2=Eni SpA 50% confirmed by 3 independent sources (offshore-technology.com, eni.com press release, and the existing mellitahog.ly Arabic company page) all describing the identical 50:50 Mellitah Oil & Gas JV. DUPLICATE CHECK against roster: NOT a duplicate. P6708 (NC 41-Mellitah Gas Pipeline) is a materially different, well-documented pipeline serving the Bahr Essalam field in Block NC-41 (~120km NW of Tripoli) — a separate concession from Structure A/E's Contractual Area D; P6708's own offshore-technology marketdata page independently gives 130km/30in for THAT pipeline, matching P6708's sheet values exactly, so P6708 is its own distinct, correctly-specified entity, not this row. P6716/P7617 (DP3-DP4-Sabratha Gas Pipeline, both) are gathering lines tying subsea wellheads to the Sabratha platform (per jpt.spe.org's Saipem/BGUP contract article, ~28km of DP3/DP4/Sabratha pipelines) — again a different, narrower segment than the Structure-E-to-shore export line. STATUS/START: construction / StartYear1=2026 corroborated by 2+ sources (offshore-technology.com verified; petrogaslibya.com 2025/2026-dated outlook piece verified, still describing the project as under construction targeting 2026 startup). See separate spec concern below — while the pipeline is real, its recorded Length and Diameter do not match the sheet's own cited source.

validity.recommendation: correct Length to ~30 km and Diameter to 36 in for the Structure E export segment (or clarify scope if 130 km is meant to represent the full field-to-Mellitah routing including tie-in to the existing Sabratha-Mellitah trunk) — current 130.00 km / 32 in are not supported by any source found, including the sheet's own citation
validity.researcher_notes: Both recorded SPEC values conflict with the sheet's own cited source (offshore-technology.com, verified live, exact tokens '36in' and '30km' both present in the page text): 'A 30km-long and 36in-diameter gas pipeline will deliver production from Structure E to an existing 36in gas export pipeline from the Sabratha Platform to the Mellitah Complex.' Neither 130 km nor 32 in appears anywhere in that source, nor in the Google-redirect URL the sheet cites for Diameter (which the sheet's own existing_ref_checks already flags as not containing '32'). The 130 km figure most likely traces to a DIFFERENT fact — 'Structure E is located in the central-eastern part of Area D, approximately 130km from the Libyan coast' (confirmed via independent search of offshore-technology/industry coverage) — i.e. the field's offshore distance from shore, not the constructed pipeline's length, which per the source is only 30 km (the new tie-in segment; it then joins an existing, separately-tracked 36in trunk from Sabratha Platform to Mellitah). 32in also does not match any segment described for this project: gas export=36in, condensate export=10in, Structure A gathering=18in, Structure E gathering (tie-back)=16in. Diameter=32in appears to be either a typo/transposition of 30 or 36, or contamination from a different row. I could not find a second fully independent, url_verifier-passing source giving the precise 36in/30km figures beyond offshore-technology.com itself (an SPE/jpt.spe.org article on a related Saipem contract discusses a different segment, DP3/DP4/Sabratha, not this one), so I'm not proposing a replacement value with high confidence — flagging as a concern for a data-team decision rather than silently 'fixing' it.

fills.researcher_notes: Not filling — the recorded value (130.00 km) itself appears wrong (see spec concern in validity above); adding a ref here would falsely imply a source supports 130 km when the only on-topic source found (offshore-technology.com) instead states 30 km for this segment. Leaving unresolved rather than fabricating support for a disputed number.

Start side is an offshore gas field (Structure E, Contractual Area D, ~130km offshore, water depth 205-235m per industry coverage) with no onshore administrative location to assign, so left StartLocation/StartPrefecture/StartState-Province blank rather than force a Libyan province onto an offshore point. On the end side, confirmed via mellitahog.ly's own Mellitah Complex page (verified live) that the complex sits '22 km east of Zwara City' -- consistent with the existing EndPrefecture/District='Mellitah', but I could not independently confirm the correct GEM controlled-vocabulary term for EndState/Province (Libya's district/shabiya naming is inconsistent across sources) with a non-wiki citation, so left it unresolved rather than guess.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=construction still holds. petrogaslibya.com's 2026 outlook piece (content references an October-2025-dated related Sabratha compression project, so effectively current to late 2025/early 2026) still describes Structures A&E as scheduled to start production in 2026 ('end of 2026 timing' referenced), i.e. not yet operating. No news found of FID reversal, cancellation, or early startup. Consistent with StartYear1=2026 already on the sheet. Well within normal construction timelines for an FID (Jan 2023) to first-gas (2026) window, so no staleness concern.

summary: E Structure-Mellitah Gas Pipeline is a real, correctly-classified, Eni/NOC-owned gas export line for the Structures A&E offshore development, on track for 2026 startup per current sources -- but its recorded Length (130.00 km) and Diameter (32 in) both conflict with the sheet's own cited source, which instead states a 30 km, 36-in pipeline (130 km appears to be the field's offshore distance from the coast, misapplied as pipeline length).
